top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, Lightforce, Spark, Angel, suresmile, clearcorrect, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, twin brackets, traditional fixed braces, SLB, damon ultima brackets
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, rentability, time saving, staff efficiency, diary changes, practice optimisation, appointment reduction, emergencies reduction, adaptive aligner change, dynamic scheduling, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, efficiency in bracket systems, bonding failures, door breakage, debond rates, torque efficiency, performance in NHS Hospital environment, practice differentiation
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save time or money, or that it will meaningfully reduce appointments or staff workload. Some believe the workflow changes are not worth the effort, or that DM is only useful for aligners, not braces. Others question whether the investment will pay off in increased profitability or efficiency.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
Explain to that prospect what integrating DM means concretely for them and their team
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Resources that explore the benefits of self-ligating bracket monitoring and using insights with braces
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific ROI and efficiency data, especially for braces and mixed appliance practices. Evidence directly comparing DM-monitored workflows to standard recall in diverse practice settings is limited.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI for clinical monitoring and diagnosis versus human assessment
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of bracket debonding detection, occlusal assessment, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, accuracy of SmartSTL, accuracy of scanning, class I goal, AI versus orthodontist, AI algorithm principle
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is as accurate as a human clinician, especially for detecting clinical changes or emergencies. Some express distrust or fear of AI, worrying about missed issues or over-reliance on automation.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, clinical study
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
I have a doctor who doesn't trust the accuracy of the AI.  I'd like to receive information regarding the accuracy.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
top_needs.gap_assessment: More head-to-head studies comparing AI findings to orthodontist assessments, especially for specific clinical events (e.g., debonding, passivity, eruption), are needed. Evidence for SmartSTL’s accuracy is also in demand.

top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are unsure if patients will actually like or comply with DM, or if it will improve their experience. Some worry about increased burden or reduced personal connection, while others question if staff will accept the new workflow.

top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct comparative studies on refinement rates and tracking outcomes with and without DM, especially across multiple aligner brands, are limited and should be prioritized.
